theme: 3 terms on handling user input in UIKit: a control calling a chosen method, an object that detects touches on a view, and the line of objects an event travels along

terms.definition: A pattern where a control calls a chosen method on a chosen object when an event happens.
terms.example: Wire the save button with Target Action in `viewDidLoad`.

terms.definition: An object you attach to a view to detect touches like taps, swipes or pinches.
terms.example: Add a Gesture Recognizer for the double tap, the image should zoom.
terms.code:
let tap = UITapGestureRecognizer(
    target: self, action: #selector(close))
imageView.isUserInteractionEnabled = true
imageView.addGestureRecognizer(tap)

terms.definition: The line of objects UIKit passes an event or action along until one of them handles it.
terms.example: Leave the target `nil`, the Responder Chain will find the editor.

video.title: Target Action, Gesture Recognizer & Responder Chain | Day 92
video.description:
Learn to explain how UIKit handles taps and actions: Target Action, Gesture Recognizer & Responder Chain, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Target Action - A pattern where a control calls a chosen method on a chosen object when an event happens.
Gesture Recognizer - An object you attach to a view to detect touches like taps, swipes or pinches.
Responder Chain - The line of objects UIKit passes an event or action along until one of them handles it.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Target Action - A pattern where a control calls a chosen method on a chosen object when an event happens.
한국어: 타깃 액션: 이벤트가 생기면 컨트롤이 정해진 객체의 정해진 메서드를 호출하는 패턴

landscape.hook: You tap the photo and nothing happens. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Why won't the photo open?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, tapping `photoView` does nothing. The Gesture Recognizer never fires.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Image views ignore touches by default. Set `isUserInteractionEnabled` to true.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh. And the Target Action is right? `self` with `openPhoto`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. The Gesture Recognizer calls `openPhoto` on `self` when the tap ends.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Could I use a button with Target Action instead?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sure, and a button works better with VoiceOver too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What happens if the target is `nil`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: UIKit walks the Responder Chain, from the first responder up to the app, until something handles it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. With a nil target, the Responder Chain finds who handles the action.

dialogue.code:
let tap = UITapGestureRecognizer(
    target: self,
    action: #selector(openPhoto))
photoView.addGestureRecognizer(tap)

lines.text: Button tapped, method called, that's Target Action.
